pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae Ia q.56 a.1
pairs.question: Utrum angelus cognoscat seipsum?
pairs.answer: Angelus autem, cum sit immaterialis, est quaedam forma subsistens, et per hoc intelligibilis actu. Unde sequitur quod per suam formam, quae est sua substantia, seipsum intelligat.
pairs.derivation: The article heading 'Utrum angelus cognoscat seipsum' is the genuine interrogative posed and answered by the author (scholastic authorial-rhetorical form). Answer drawn from the conclusion of the Respondeo (line 36): I skipped the long expository body of the Respondeo (the obiectum/forma analysis from 'Respondeo dicendum quod, sicut ex supra dictis patet...' through 'quam calefacit inhaerens') as non-answering setup, and started the answer at the operative concluding sentences 'Angelus autem, cum sit immaterialis...' which directly state that the angel, being immaterial, is a subsisting form and so understands itself through its form. Ended at the final full stop ('seipsum intelligat.'), where the article body turns to the Ad primum replies.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae Ia q.56 a.3
pairs.question: Utrum angeli per sua naturalia Deum cognoscere possint?
pairs.answer: Angeli aliquam cognitionem de Deo habere possunt per sua naturalia.
pairs.derivation: The article heading 'Utrum angeli per sua naturalia Deum cognoscere possint' is the genuine interrogative the author poses and answers. Answer is the opening operative sentence of the Respondeo (line 66): I dropped only the 'Respondeo dicendum quod' framing tag and ended at the first full stop, before the explanatory 'Ad cuius evidentiam, considerandum est...' digression on the threefold modes of cognition. This sentence directly answers the question in the affirmative.
